questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight hours, you should:

options.text: Not ride during the day.
Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder and stay out of traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Can be fatal.
Are never serious.
Rarely cause injuries.
Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds under 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can cause serious injuries or death.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can improve their visibility by:

options.text: Wearing darkly-colored clothing.
Turning off their headlight.
Following another vehicle very closely.
Wearing brightly-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing brightly-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing with reflective materials so other drivers can see you. Always use your headlight, signals, and brake light.

questions.question: The best lane position is:

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that allows you to draft off of other vehicles.
The one that allows you to be seen by other motorists.
The one that places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that allows you to be seen by other motorists.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and allows them to see you. Avoid blind spots and road hazards. Stay away from places where wind blasts are strong. Keep enough space to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it's warm out.
Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
Wear shorts in warm weather.
Not be concerned about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: To provide the best protection, a helmet should:

options.text: Have a few cracks.
Not be certified.
Have frayed straps.
Fit snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Provides protection in a crash.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides protection in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, ideally leather, when riding. A leather jacket protects you in a crash and helps prevent dehydration in warm weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Allow them to pass.
Prevent them from passing.
Move to one side of your lane to allow them to share the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate faster.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, the operator should:

options.text: Maintain a longer following distance.
Increase their speed.
Deflate the tires to accommodate the extra weight.
Not warn passengers of impending hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a longer following distance.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger's weight. Keep a larger space cushion between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: It is best to not ride directly alongside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be riding in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be difficult to see what is happening behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be riding in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside a vehicle in another lane is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. They won't know you're there. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What color are warning signs, and what color is the lettering?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Can proper clothing help protect you in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing is not really for protection.
No, clothing is more of a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces injury in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. They should be made of sturdy material and fit snugly so they do not flap.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Be close to the road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. It helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, their blind spots, and road hazards. It also prevents other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What should you remember about motorcycle blind spots in traffic?

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots that are too small to cause any problems.
Have blind spots that require head checks.
Have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that require head checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: You have had drinks. If you wait one hour per drink before riding, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Side effects from the drinking may still remain.
You will be okay as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side effects from the drinking may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. Your ability and judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: When should you keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver in front of you from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions will make stopping more difficult than usual.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space when your motorcycle needs more time to stop. This includes slippery pavement, when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and drivers may cut in front of you.

questions.question: When braking your motorcycle, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes.
Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time. They work best together.

questions.question: What happens when you take a turn too fast on a motorcycle?

options.text: Is acceptable as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is acceptable as long as no vehicles are near you.
Can cause you to end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may not be able to hold the turn and could drift into another lane or off the road. Use caution when turning.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Try to blend into traffic and not be noticed by other drivers.
Not use turn signals unless you are traveling at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride closely to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by being visible to others. Use turn signals, use your brake light, and position your motorcycle correctly. Keep safe distance, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position your motorcycle in the lane?

options.text: In any part of the lane.
In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
In the part of the lane that places your image in the car's rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of the lane that places your image in the car's rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually this means the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors often, so this position makes it more likely they will see you.
